chapter: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
title: How many tunes, and what happened to his last five
summary: He cannot say how many tunes he wrote or list them; the last five or six went to Mills and he has heard nothing since the company was sold.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How many tunes did you write? Do you know?

Oh, gosh -- quite a bit. It didn't amount to much, but still, they come, and the checks come -- like I said before, they come in amounts of two, three, five dollars. "Lost in Meditation" should have been a good tune, if they only plugged it like they should have. "Perdido" sold a lot with -- who's that girl, that colored girl? Sarah Vaughn. Oh gosh, she did a good job with it.
Do you have a list of all of your compositions, the names of all the tunes you have written?

You know, believe me when I tell you I don't have nothing. I don't have nothing like that. When they send me the piece of paper, when I got the bills, the amounts and what I receive and what I'm supposed to get, I'd get the names of all the tunes that they got that belong to me, and they are in the contract, or whatever you call it.

But really, I don't know exactly how many tunes I wrote. I wrote five or six tunes; the last six tunes I wrote, I gave it to Mills, and they are now someplace out of town. The publishers or something, because they're still on Broadway, aren't they?
Mills sold his company to another
company. Irving Mills doesn't have it any more. And now I think it's Mills Belwin Music.
Well, his brother was a best big publisher.
His son was in it, too.

But these five tunes, I wrote, and I think I recorded them with a small group. Didn't come out to anything, but still, I didn't hear anything from the Mills Music Company. I guess when I die, they'll bring it out.
